Now when Abd al-Masih saw
that the whole populace was inclined after Nur al-Din,
he feared lest he should take him by the sword.
He sent asking for a pledge of safe conduct for his life,
that he might surrender Mosul to him,
provided, however, that he would not take it away from Sayf al-Din.
Nur al-Din, however, replied:
"I have not come to seize a city or kingdom from my brother's sons,
but to deliver the weak from your oppression,
O Abd al-Masih.
Therefore, more than that I leave you alive,
and remove you from Mosul,
and take you with me to Syria,
do not expect from me."
And so peace was made.
And Nur al-Din entered Mosul,
and took up residence in its fortress.
And he left Sayf al-Din Ghazi as lord of Mosul just as he had been.
And in the citadel he appointed a dizdar,
that is, a governor,
a certain eunuch whose name was Sa'd al-Din Kumishtakin
(Gumushtekin?),
and the possessions which his brother had left,
he divided equally among his sons.
And he remitted many taxes for the people.
And he built the Great Mosque
which is called the Nuri [Mosque].
And to Sayf al-Din, in addition to Mosul, he also added Jazirat Qardu [Jazirat Ibn 'Umar].
And when he had remained in Mosul seventeen
days,
he returned to Syria,
and with him Fakhr al-Din Abd al-Masih.
And he changed his name and called him Abdallah,
and gave him other abundant revenues.
This Abd al-Masih, although in outward appearance he showed himself a Muslim,
in his inner person he served Christianity,
and did great good deeds for the Christians,
and was an open hater of the Arabs and their teachers.
And the blessed Patriarch Mar Michael compares him to Mordecai.
And in this year the Caliph al-Mustanjid fell ill with the disease of colic.
And when the illness grew severe upon him,
some of the magnates, the ustaddar and others, despaired of his life,
and they opened the door of the prison,
and brought out their imprisoned brothers.
The vizier, however, sent and informed the Caliph.
And the Caliph was enraged,
and ordered the Christian physician who was Ibn Safiyya, who was with him,
to write to the vizier
to subdue these magnates
and cut off their heads.
